title: LLM reading digest — March 2026 (scratchpad)
content:
Quick personal digest of recent papers/blogs/demos I skimmed — lightweight notes, half-formed ideas, and tasks. Mostly for my future self; messy.

Reading list (short):
- "FlashAttention 2" blog + arXiv (latest optimizations for memory/throughput) — read 2026-02-18. Key: fused kernels + memory scheduling for long contexts. Curious about how this interacts with continuous batching in our runtime.
- "KV cache partitioning for multi-tenant inference" (workshop notes) — 2026-01-06. Small experiments indicate partitioned KV gives predictable isolation, but throughput drop is nontrivial when shards are small.
- "Adaptive quantization for LLMs in production" (industrial blog, Dec 2025) — good heuristics on per-layer quant levels and dynamic fallback. Tied to Redwood Optimize ideas.
- NeurIPS 2025 poster: "Prefix caching policies for dialog workloads" — short poster, interesting metric: 'cache-hit utility' (combines perplexity delta + latency gain).

Summaries + quick takeaways:
- FlashAttention 2
  - Implementation notes: kernel fusion reduces global memory traffic. For seq lengths > 4k, speedups are huge. But the kernel assumes contiguous KV layout — our KV cache with sharded slices may need a rework to keep contiguity.
  - Experiment idea: proto bench with Llama-2-70b quantized to 4-bit and FA2 kernels on A100 vs H100. Focus: tail latency at 95/99p for chat workloads.

- KV cache partitioning
  - Tradeoff: better multi-tenant isolation vs throughput loss on sub-batch sizes. Maybe we can combine partitioning with dynamic coalescing: combine idle tenants' shards into ephemeral coalesced batches for throughput, but preserve logical isolation in control plane.
  - Open Q: implications for security/audit logs when coalescing — must ensure no cross-tenant data leakage; scope with Security.

- Adaptive quantization
  - Per-layer sensitivity profiling at offline time, then a small RL/heuristic at runtime to flip layers between q4/q8 for cold vs hot requests.
  - Risk: quality regressions on rare prompts. Proposed mitigation: shadow inference with higher precision for a small percent and automatic rollback alerts in Optimize.

Conference takeaways (In-person notes scribble):
- Talk: "Operationalizing fallbacks" — the thing I keep coming back to: fallback policies must be measurable in user-facing metrics (not just token loss). Maps well to Redwood Console rollout dashboards.
- Panel: "Edge and private inference": customers want reproducible performance and predictable cost. Private deployment interest is high — aligns with sales signal for Private.

Loose experiments to run (priority ordering):
1) Small bench harness: run FA2 kernels vs current runtime dispatch for 2 model sizes (7B, 70B) on A100 and H100. Capture 50/95/99p latencies for single-stream and batched workloads. (Owner: me; duration: 2 weeks)
2) KV coalescing prototype: scheduler that detects idle tenant shards and coalesces them for ephemeral batch windows; safety: zero-copy read-only combine, maintain audit stamps. Quick sim with synthetic traces. (Pair w/ Ethan)
3) Quantization fallback: implement shadow-10% route where we also run high-precision path in background for a subset of requests (costly but useful to detect regressions). Hook into existing eval set and quality monitors in Console.

Notes-to-self / half thoughts:
- When writing docs, emphasize "unit economics" impacts: how much per-token saved vs added tail latency for users. Product cares more than raw throughput improvements.
- Need to capture workloads: 'chat streaming' vs 'generate large passage' shapes cache and batching differently. Add examples to the bench harness config.
- Remember to check the PR #412 on runtime: patches to the kernel loader might conflict with FA2 assumptions.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Can we maintain zero-copy KV layout and still use FA2 fused kernels? If not, cost of reshuffling might erase speedups.
- How to quantify cache-hit utility in a cost-aware way? Metric proposal: delta_cost_per_response = baseline_cost - cached_cost adjusted by quality penalty.
- Is ephemeral coalescing acceptable for certain enterprise SLAs? Need to consult SRE and Sales for allowed variance.

Links + quick refs (to save for later):
- FA2 blog: https://example.org/flashattention2 (bookmark)
- ArXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08774 — re-check math on memory complexity.
- Internal runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 (important: loader changes)
- Slack thread re: KV-slicing: slack://thread/CF5K2J3E8-1623

Action items (concrete):
- [ ] Kick off bench harness ticket in GH (title: "bench: FA2 vs runtime dispatch - microbench") — assign to me.
- [ ] Draft brief for Security about coalescing model (outline risk and controls) — ping Priya.
- [ ] Add cache-hit utility metric to Console backlog (contact product-hosted-api).

Rough timeline: experiments 2–4 weeks, follow-up doc summarizing results and recommendations for Optimize.

End of scratchpad. Keep this lightweight — will tidy into a proper doc if experiments worth pursuing.
